text.p: Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc said on Monday its 225-bank syndicate had approved the extension of the debt standstill date to December 14, 1997 from March 14, 1997.
Last October, Eurotunnel and its banks agreed a restructuring deal for the debt-laden group. Eurotunnel said the standstill originally began in September 1995 and was allowed to run until March.
Last October, following marathon negotiations, Eurotunnel and the steering committee of banks agreed a restructuring deal which will have to approved by 225 creditor banks and shareholders.
In January, bankers in London said they hoped to sign a package restructuring Eurotunnel's 8.7 billion pounds ($14.2 billion) debt well before a new year-end deadline expired.
The standstill extension will have no effect on the debt deal, which will continue to apply to Eurotunnel's debt position at October 15, 1996, bankers said in January.

Eurotunnel was hit by a fire last November in the Channel tunnel but said in January that business was returning strongly and the company expected to have 50 percent of the Channel market by year-end.
